name: Georgia
summary: A Caucasus country with an ancient Christian kingdom tradition, independent from the USSR in 1991; Abkhazia and South Ossetia are outside its control.

knownFor.label: Georgian alphabet
knownFor.note: Its own script, used since the 5th century.

knownFor.label: Qvevri wine
knownFor.note: Wine made in clay jars, about 8,000 years old.

location.value: The Caucasus region, on the east coast of the Black Sea; about 67,900 km².

terrain.value: The Greater Caucasus range in the north and the Lesser Caucasus highlands in the south.

climate.value: Very diverse: humid subtropical in the west, changing to continental in the east; colder in the mountains.

resources.value: Sizeable hydropower resources; vineyards for wine.

disasters.value: Earthquakes (Racha, 1991), landslides and floods, such as the 2015 Tbilisi flood.

urbanisation.value: Over a third of people live in Tbilisi, the capital and largest city.

disease.value: Moderate health; tuberculosis and hepatitis C were serious problems, tackled by national programmes.

migration.value: The 2008 war displaced 192,000 people, though many later returned.

economicBase.value: Mostly services (59% of GDP in 2016), with tourism and wine-making important.

tradeRoutes.value: A transport corridor through the ports of Batumi and Poti, the Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan oil pipeline and the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country, still poorer than most of Europe.

moneyAndTax.value: The lari, introduced in 1995 after hyperinflation.

inequality.value: Moderate, with poorer rural areas and many people relying on money sent from abroad.

keyRulers.value: Zviad Gamsakhurdia. Eduard Shevardnadze. Mikheil Saakashvili.

succession.value: Elections; the 2012 election was the first peaceful electoral transfer of power.

institutions.value: Parliament, the government, the Constitutional Court and the Georgian Orthodox Church as an influential body.

stability.value: Civil war (to 1993); the peaceful Rose Revolution (2003); a deep political crisis since October 2024.

eliteConflict.value: A highly polarised political and media climate.

armyAndTech.value: Up to 2,000 soldiers served in Iraq; 1,560 in Afghanistan in 2013, the largest non-NATO contributor.

majorWars.value: Civil war (to 1993), secessionist wars in Abkhazia and South Ossetia, and the Russo-Georgian War (2008).

territoryChange.value: Since the 2008 war, parts of Abkhazia and South Ossetia have been controlled by Russian-backed separatists, with Russian military bases.

alliancesRivals.value: Seeks EU and NATO membership; EU candidate status (December 2023); worsening relations with Russia.

inventions.value: Hosts the world’s earliest known sites of winemaking (about 6000 BCE).

scienceEducation.value: Tbilisi State University (founded 1918) and other universities; high literacy.

openness.value: Reforms since 2003 created one of the freest business climates in the world; visa-free EU travel for Georgians since 2017.

communicationTransport.value: The Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway (opened 2017) links the Caucasus with Turkey.

religion.value: About 82% Eastern Orthodox Christian, mostly in the Georgian Orthodox Church.

languageWriting.value: Georgian, part of the small Kartvelian family, unrelated to any other language family.

artsArchitecture.value: Gelati Monastery and Bagrati Cathedral (UNESCO sites), and an early tradition of polyphonic singing.

socialStructure.value: Strong family networks; a gap between Tbilisi and rural areas.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong national identity built on the Georgian language, Orthodox Christianity and a long history of resisting empires.

neighbours.value: Russia to the north, Turkey and Armenia to the south, Azerbaijan to the south-east.

ideasReligions.value: King Mirian III made Christianity the state religion of Iberia in 337.

colonisation.value: Annexed by the Russian Empire from 1801; independent 1918–21; then a Soviet republic until 1991.

riseSignals.value: Declared independence from the Soviet Union in April 1991.

peakPeriod.value: Reforms after the 2003 Rose Revolution eradicated low-level corruption and freed up business.

declineSignals.value: Russia recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia (2008); Georgia and most countries regard them as occupied.
